scores.worst_problem: The hook withholds detail but not shape — "year four explains why" telegraphs a patience-compounds arc that a reader can guess before swiping, so the deck confirms rather than reveals.
scores.fix: Rewrite slide 1 so the gap is a contradiction rather than a timeline, e.g. lead with the specific thing the slow year cost you or the deal you refused, so the reader cannot pre-write the lesson.

points.title: Four Houses. That Was It.
body: Everyone who started when I did wanted a huge first year.
I wanted a year I could copy and paste.
points.loop: Copying it cost me things I liked.

points.title: Ninety Minutes, Every Morning
body: Same block, same three tasks. Calls, follow ups, notes.
Boring on a Tuesday. Undefeated over two years.
points.loop: Then the money showed up and lied.

points.title: I Paid Myself Last
body: Every check funded the business first. Taxes, marketing, six months of runway.
Whatever survived that was mine to spend.
points.loop: The runway got used sooner than planned.

points.title: The Listing I Turned Down
body: Wrong price, seller would not move, and I needed the check.
I told him no and drove home sick about it.
points.loop: That no showed up on paper later.

points.title: Year Four
body: The pipeline started feeding itself. Repeat clients, referrals, people who remembered I told them the truth.
Four houses in year one built the thing that runs now.

linkedinCaption:
Four houses in my first year. That was the whole scoreboard.

I stopped chasing a big first year and started building one I could repeat. Ninety minutes every morning on the same three tasks. Calls, follow ups, notes. Dull on a Tuesday. It never lost over two years.

I paid the business before I paid myself. Taxes, marketing, six months of runway. What survived was mine.

I turned down a listing I needed because the price was wrong and the seller would not move. I drove home sick about it. It was still the right call.

Year four, the pipeline feeds itself. Repeat clients and referrals from people who remembered I told them the truth.

What did you turn down early that paid you back later?
